comparison: Perfect agreement on C21-C23. Reviewers describe the work as 'solid' and do not question these foundational measurements.

Perfect agreement on C24-C26. Both evaluations support the RNA-seq findings showing shared and unique gene expression patterns across treatments. Reviewers explicitly acknowledge the 'considerable effort in comparing transcriptome data' and accept these findings as valid and central to the manuscript.

Strong agreement on C27-C30 (vermiculite drying phenotype). OpenEval focuses on these specific claims while peer review groups them with C31-C34 (transcriptomic responses). Both evaluations support the vermiculite drying as a valid reference condition with appropriate physiological and molecular characterization.

Strong agreement on C31-C34 (vermiculite transcriptomic responses and reversibility). OpenEval evaluates these separately while peer review combines them with C27-C30. Both find the transcriptomic data and reversibility upon rewatering well-supported and methodologically sound.

Agreement on C38-C39 regarding directional agreement in shoots. OpenEval covers broader claims (C38-C44) including marker genes and amplitude differences, while peer review focuses on C38-C39 and C80 (summary claim). Both treat the shoot directional agreement as a key positive finding.

Partial overlap on C40-C44 (marker gene expression and amplitude differences). OpenEval groups these with shoot directional agreement claims, while peer review evaluates them separately alongside C45-C46 (speculative explanations). Both accept the marker gene data and authors' cautious interpretation of amplitude differences.

Strong agreement on C47-C49, C52-C53 regarding poor directional agreement in roots. OpenEval covers C47-C53 while peer review adds C81 (summary claim). Both evaluations recognize this as a central, well-demonstrated finding showing tissue-specific variability across methods.

Both evaluations positively assess HA's physiological and transcriptomic validation, with reviewers highlighting it as a methodological contribution with improved root directional agreement.

Perfect agreement on C65-C75. Both evaluations support the mechanistic dissection showing agar strength and nutrient concentration both contribute to HA effects. Reviewers explicitly acknowledge this analysis as strengthening the HA assay characterization.

Perfect agreement on C76-C79. Both evaluations support the correlation between HA phenotypes and field fitness data. OpenEval notes the modest p-value (0.04) suggesting replication would be beneficial, while reviewers view it as 'promising' and supporting high-throughput screening utility.

Partial overlap on summary claim C80. OpenEval groups C80-C82 as supported summary claims, while peer review mentions C80 alongside C38-C39 (shoot directional agreement). Both treat these high-level conclusions as accurately reflecting the experimental findings.

Partial overlap on summary claim C81. OpenEval groups C80-C82 together while peer review mentions C81 with root directional agreement findings (C47-C49, C52-C53). Both accept this summary as consistent with demonstrated results.
